title: PCA
description: Linear dimensionality reduction technique project data along principal components.
name: PCA
summary: PCA (Principal Component Analysis) orthogonalizes high-dimensional feature spaces by finding the directions (principal components) that maximize variance, projecting the data into fewer dimensions.
use_when: Reducing feature dimensions to speed up downstream models or visualize high-dimensional data linearly.
avoid_when: Underlying relationships are highly non-linear, as PCA is limited to linear projection.
pros: Significantly reduces multicollinearity in downstream models.
Extremely fast to compute using Singular Value Decomposition (SVD).
Saves storage and memory by discarding low-variance components.
cons: Principal components are linear combinations, making them hard to interpret physically.
Can lose valuable predictive information if it resides in low-variance components.
Highly sensitive to feature scales, requiring prior standardization.

key_hyperparams.name: n_components
key_hyperparams.note: Number of components to keep. If not set, all components are kept.

quick_start:
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
import numpy as np

X = np.array([[-1, -1], [-2, -1], [-3, -2], [1, 1], [2, 1], [3, 2]])
pca = PCA(n_components=2)
pca.fit(X)
reduced = pca.transform(X)
